title: Tenant priority reservation and graceful hosted overflow orchestration
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and implement a tenant-aware overflow orchestration that reserves short-duration capacity windows for high-priority tenants on Dedicated pools and applies a staged, latency-preserving migration to Hosted when Dedicated capacity is constrained. Goals: (1) avoid disruptive bulk spillover that causes p99 latency regressions for high-priority workloads, (2) allow predictable preemption policies for bursty tenants, (3) provide a deterministic model-variant downgrade matrix for cost-aware fallbacks, and (4) surface observability and runbook steps for operators.
acceptance_criteria: API and router can accept per-tenant reservation tokens and honor reservation windows (soft + hard) when scheduling to Dedicated pools
When Dedicated pool free slots < threshold, router triggers staged overflow for affected tenants to Hosted with concurrency ramp and rate-limits to maintain latency SLOs
Preemption ordering implemented: (1) best-effort tenants, (2) low-priority reserved tenants beyond grace window, (3) evictable background workloads. Admin-visible eviction logs produced
Fallback model variant matrix applied per-tenant: primary -> quantized-variant -> distilled-variant, with configurable quality thresholds and cost deltas
Telemetry: per-tenant overflow events, preemption_count, reservation_misses, p50/p95/p99 latency delta, hosted-cost delta. Dashboards and alerts created
Canary rollout plan documented and executed with 10% traffic, rollback on >5% regression to p99 or >20% cost delta
